question: Should this PR land the direct Computer Use MCP probe exception, fail-closed readiness default, periodic stale-child repair, lease surface, shared Codex.app cache default, and seven new config/default knobs together?
rationale: The implementation appears functionally sound, but the branch changes sandbox-adjacent native app-server calls, host process cleanup, custom-marketplace cache policy, and upgrade-visible defaults, which requires maintainer intent rather than automated correctness judgment.

options.title: Approve Current Scope After Owner Review
options.body: Accept the stricter readiness, MCP probe exception, repair, lease, health, shared cache, and config defaults as the intended Computer Use contract before merge.

options.title: Split Risky Surfaces
options.body: Land cache reconciliation and live status first, then review process repair, lease management, and config defaults in narrower PRs.

options.title: Narrow Defaults Before Merge
options.body: Keep compatibility as the default and make fail-closed repair or health behavior opt-in until upgrade impact is proven more broadly.

recommendation.title: Approve Current Scope After Owner Review
recommendation.body: Accept the stricter readiness, MCP probe exception, repair, lease, health, shared cache, and config defaults as the intended Computer Use contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership evidence points to the active Codex app-server files where the security-boundary and default behavior now live.
